subject: Multi-region SLO & routing — post-call checklist and ops next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@finlytics.com>, Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@finlytics.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 14:05:00 -0500
Subject: Multi-region SLO & routing — post-call checklist and ops next steps

Hi Laura / Rajiv — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have aligned expectations on performance and residency before we scope a pilot: 

Recap (from your ask on the call):
- Traffic: primary users in US and EU, smaller APAC presence (Tokyo office)
- Target SLOs: p95 latency targets for typical 128-token responses; streaming start-of-response latency for interactive UI
- Throughput / concurrency: sustained average ~120 RPS, peak concurrent sessions ~300, daily tokens ~1M (estimate)
- Data residency: EU customer data must remain in EU for at-rest logs and audit trails; some EU users need all metadata pinned to EU region

Ben's proposed checklist / asks for the perf run: 
1) Confirm p95 latency targets you want us to validate in each region (suggested: US/EU = 150ms p95 for 128-token non-streaming; APAC = 250ms p95).
2) Streaming requirements: what is the expected first-byte/start-of-stream threshold (we typically measure TTFB and per-chunk latency). Suggested: first chunk p50 < 40ms, subsequent chunk p95 < 80ms.
3) Traffic profile: attach a short sample payload + RPS profile (we need percentiles and concurrency distribution).
4) Network / security constraints: which CIDR ranges should we expect for egress/ingress, and do you need an IP allowlist for dedicated endpoints?
5) Data residency confirmation: which artifacts must remain in-region (raw request logs, token-level traces, aggregated metrics?).

Next steps (proposed):
- Monica (CS/AM) to share mutual action plan (attached).
- Tessa (SE) to propose perf run plan and required samples; we will schedule a 2-hour perf window in your preferred regions (US-East, eu-west, ap-northeast).
- Finlytics to confirm SLO numbers & provide sample traffic by EOD Thursday (2026-02-19).

If those items look good I’ll schedule the perf run and loop in infra for IP allowlisting.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales 
Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: 20260218-finlytics-map-mutual-action-plan.pdf, network-egress-topology.png

From: Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@finlytics.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@finlytics.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 16:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Multi-region SLO & routing — post-call checklist and ops next steps

Thanks Ben — quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Latency SLOs: we can confirm approximate targets:
   - US & EU: p95 end-to-end <= 150ms for 128-token completions (non-streaming).
   - APAC (Tokyo): p95 <= 220ms (we're willing to accept slightly higher).

2) Streaming: our UX relies on fast first-chunk for interactive typing hints. Please treat first-byte (start-of-stream) separately. Goal: p50 start-of-stream < 40ms, p95 per-chunk <= 90ms.

3) Throughput: your suggested numbers are close. Our telemetry expects peaks at ~200 RPS during market open; concurrency spikes to ~350 for short bursts. Daily token volume is probably closer to 1.2M.

4) Data residency: EU regulation requires that raw request logs and request metadata for EU users remain in-region. Aggregated metrics can be copied out for global dashboards only if anonymized. No cross-border retention of identifiable logs from EU users.

5) Benchmarks: please provide a short report with baseline numbers for the model family you recommended (we discussed the 'redwood-xf-16' family) from the three regions. Include p50/p95/p99 and streaming TTFB.

We can share a sample traffic JSON by tomorrow morning. Please include a short statement on how your routing will respect data residency and whether egress to a central metrics store would be optional.

— Rajiv
Head of Platform Engineering, Finlytics
rajiv.singh@finlytics.com

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@finlytics.com>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@finlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 17:01:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Multi-region SLO & routing — post-call checklist and ops next steps

Thanks — a few engineering notes based on the targets above: 

- Model & config: redwood-xf-16 in 8-bit quantized mode should meet the latency targets on dedicated VMs with region-local GPUs. For hosted/shared capacity we'll need to evaluate tail latency under cross-tenant load.
- Batching & streaming: continuous batching helps throughput but increases tail latency for low-concurrency interactive requests. We can prioritize latency by tuning batching windows for low-latency routes (per-route config). Streaming TTFB is mostly bounded by network RTT + model decode first-token; we should instrument TTFB in the perf run.
- Routing & residency: we support policy-based routing: route by geo-IP → region-local model variants. For EU users you can pin sessions to eu-west endpoints; logs can be configured to stay in-region (we can set retention and disable cross-region metrics exports). We will need a short data-processing addendum for guaranteed in-region log residency for EU users if this is required contractually.
- Run plan: propose a 2-hour perf window that includes:
   * Synthetic traffic for US/EU/APAC with your sample payloads (we'll replay at target RPS & concurrency).
   * Streaming and non-streaming scenarios.
   * Collection of p50/p95/p99, TTFB, and token throughput.

What we need from Finlytics to run:
- Sample traffic JSON (RPS curve + payload size distribution) — upload to the Drive link in Ben's email.
- A list of allowed CIDR ranges if you want IP-restricted endpoints.
- Confirmation whether we should run on Hosted API endpoints or spin up Dedicated pools in each region (Dedicated will give tighter SLOs).

I can own the perf run and produce a short report (1–2 pages) with recommendation (config, model variant, quantization) and expected cost delta.

— Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
